 GOAL Winners and losers: Christian Pulisic bags a brace as Manchester United-bound Mauricio Pochettino begins USMNT farewell with 6-0 Haiti rout
 GOAL breaks down the big takeaways from Saturday's 6-0 USMNT win over Haiti.
 Ryan Tolmich 57 minutes ago Last updated 55 minutes ago Share Share MIAMI -- Are you sure you want to leave, Mauricio Pochettino? Why head to Manchester when the U.S. Men's National Team are having this much fun? Saturday's CONCACAF Nations League performance against Haiti made a pretty good case for sticking around.
 The U.S. rolled to a 6-0 win, with returning stars Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie all finding the net. Pulisic scored twice, while Auston Trusty and Julian Hall also got on the scoresheet. Five goals came after halftime, four from the returning trio, as the U.S. built on the momentum of its four wins across September and October.
 All of that even though the build-up to Saturday's game in Miami had nothing to do with Saturday's game in Miami. All eyes, from America to Manchester, were always on Pochettino , who said that he was going to see out these two games to leave on the right sort of note. A 6-0 first-leg win is more than right; it's ideal. And, even taking into account the opposition, this was among the more free-flowing stretches of USMNT soccer in this Poch era.
 That era ends Tuesday, giving Pochettino one more game to savor before heading to Manchester. If the U.S. produce anything close to Saturday’s performance, he’ll get the send-off he wanted. Friday’s tears may return when it’s time to say goodbye, but another display like this would give him plenty to smile about, too.
 GOAL breaks down the winners and losers of the USMNT's win...
 WINNER: Christian Pulisic
 Getty Images Sport The American star got a brace that should feel like a weight off his shoulders.
 For 60-ish minutes, Haiti kept Pulisic somewhat quiet in the USMNT star’s first post-World Cup game. A penalty, awarded after he was brought down in the box following Julian Hall’s backheel, changed everything. Pulisic converted in the 62nd minute, then struck again a minute later. Suddenly, he had two goals to his name.
 Pulisic’s second goal was even better than his first. Less than a minute after converting his penalty, he scored from open play with a shot from just outside the box. After the penalty, he had run over to celebrate with family. This time, there was just a smile, as if he hadn’t had time to plan another celebration.
 Scoring was reason enough to celebrate, though. So many eyes were on the USMNT star given how this World Cup ended and, although this wasn't as dominant a performance as the goals will indicate, it was one that ultimately resulted in a brace. It'll take more than a brace to start building back the vibes heading into this cycle, though, but this was a pretty nice start for a player that needed exactly that.
 WINNER: Mauricio Pochettino
 Getty Images Sport There was no post-announcement hangover for Pochettino's team.
 With a sold-out crowd in Miami and countless eyes watching from across the pond in Manchester, Pochettino's side delivered. Losing against Haiti, theoretically, wouldn't have impacted his arrival at Manchester United, but it wouldn't have looked good, would it? No concerns there, though.
 Just one day after it was announced that Pochettino was bound for Old Trafford, the USMNT played without any sort of hangover effects. Whether Pochettino's departure added any extra motivation, only the players can say. At the very least, it's safe to say that Pochettino had those players ready to play and, in the end, ready to put a beating on an overmatched Haiti team.
 For the USMNT, that's great. For those in Manchester watching, it provided some reason for excitement. Haiti are no Liverpool, of course, but this was a fun display of Poch-ball and how, ultimately, it can lead to goals. There were plenty of those on Saturday and plenty of reasons for Pochettino to feel good about where he's leaving this team when he does inevitably leave.
 LOSER: Haiti
 Getty Images Sport A decent first half led to a total meltdown in the second.
 Heading into halftime, Haiti were losing, but they were in it. The "hosts" were down a goal, but doing relatively okay. They had one good chance of their own and conceded via a set piece on the other side. It happens.
 Then, early in the second half, it all fell apart. A 1-0 loss in the first leg is fine. 6-0? Heading to an away leg in Cincinnati? That's going to be tough to come back from.
 The USMNT's 15-minute blitz included four goals that effectively buried Les Grenadiers, giving them a hole that will almost certainly be too big to climb out of. It didn't look like it was going that way for most of the match, though. Haiti was playing well enough until, suddenly, they weren't, effectively ending their hopes of winning the game and the tie.
 Tuesday is little more than a formality now, which will be a tough pill to swallow considering how the match started.
 WINNER: Julian Hall
 Getty Images Sport Hall made it four goals in five international caps with his finish in the second half.
 Hall's starts for the USMNT have generally followed a similar script. He knocks and knocks, then knocks some more. Then, ultimately, he gets his goal, and there's never any denying how deserved it is.
 The rising young New York Red Bulls striker deserved his finish on Saturday, and the truth is that he may have deserved a few more. Before netting in the 53rd minute, Hall had one fantastic chance pushed away and one narrowly called back via an offside call. And yet, as usual, he kept threatening until he finally broke through.
 Credit to Antonee Robinson for the ball that put him through, but credit, too, to Hall for the composure. He received the ball, took a touch and finished calmly, silencing the pro-Haiti crowd so soon into the second half. That's now four in five games and four in around 300 minutes for a player who continues to make the most of his opportunities. 
 WINNER: Sebastian Berhalter
 Getty Images Sport Another game, another set piece assist from Berhalter.
 There are trade-offs made when certain players start in midfield. With Sebastian Berhalter, for example, you're giving up a little bit of ability to control the game when you start him in the center of the park.
 What you get, though, is worth it. He showed that again on Saturday.
 Berhalter's brilliant set piece set up the USMNT's first goal, leaving Auston Trusty with little more than a tap-in. Trusty got the goal, but Berhalter's free kick to the back post did all of the heavy lifting.
 It's not the first time, either. Since his USMNT emergence, Berhalter's free kicks have been a legitimate weapon for the USMNT. They've led to multiple goals and even more dangerous moments. Set pieces aren’t always sexy, but Berhalter’s deliveries can be. Just ask Trusty.
 As long as he does that, he more than justifies his place, even as a new coach prepares to come in.
